Jehoshaphat the Recorder
jeh-HOSH-uh-fat the ree-CORD-er
proper noun
Hebrew Yehoshaphat, “the LORD hath judged,” the son of Ahilud, recorder under David and Solomon.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud held the office of recorder, or remembrancer, in the courts of both David and Solomon. The recorder (in Hebrew the mazkir, “one who brings to remembrance”) was a high officer of state, keeper of the public records and chronicles of the kingdom, and a counsellor near the throne. He is named in the rolls of David’s chief officers alongside Joab over the host and the priests Zadok and Abiathar (2Sa 8:16; 20:24), and he continued in the same office under Solomon among the princes of that king’s court (1Ki 4:3). Through the changing of reigns Jehoshaphat kept his place, a steady and trusted servant who preserved the memory of the kingdom’s acts and affairs. He is to be distinguished from the later Jehoshaphat king of Judah. His name, “the LORD hath judged,” befits a keeper of records, for the writing down of a kingdom’s deeds is itself a kind of judgment, setting truth on record for the time to come. Jehoshaphat the recorder witnesses the value of faithful memory in the service of God and the state, and the honour of the man who keeps the record straight across the years.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The son of Ahilud, recorder or remembrancer in the courts of David and Solomon.

JEHOSHAPHAT THE RECORDER, the son of Ahilud, an officer of state.

He was recorder, the keeper of the chronicles of the kingdom (2Sa 8:16).

He served in this office under both David and Solomon (1Ki 4:3).

The recorder was a high counsellor near the throne.

He is distinct from the later Jehoshaphat king of Judah.

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 8:16 — "And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;"

2Sa 20:24 — "And Adoram was over the tribute: and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder:"

1Ki 4:3 — "Elihoreph and Ahiah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder."

1Ch 18:15 — "And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, recorder."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses the value of faithful memory in the service of God and state.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the honour of faithful memory. Jehoshaphat the recorder kept the chronicles of the kingdom across two reigns, preserving the truth of what was done for the time to come. The keeping of a true record is no small service; a people that forgets its history forgets the dealings of God with it, and a kingdom without faithful remembrance loses the wisdom of its past.

His name, “the LORD hath judged,” suits the office well, for the LORD Himself keeps a perfect record of all things, and a book of remembrance is written before Him for them that fear His name (Mal 3:16). The earthly recorder is a faint image of the heavenly; God forgets nothing, and the records of His servants’ lives stand sure before His throne.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name means “the LORD hath judged,” from Yeho (the LORD) and a verb to judge.

"Like Jehoshaphat the recorder, faithful memory preserves the truth of God’s dealings for the time to come."

"Jehoshaphat teaches that a people forgetting its history forgets the dealings of God with it."

"The earthly recorder images the LORD, who keeps a book of remembrance before His throne."
